description: Kernel hardening against hostile/buggy userspace (M6.5). userspace/ctests/musl_harden.c drives four checks: SpawnArgs(79) with an unmapped block -> EFAULT (not a ring-0 panic), DrawRect(12) from a non-owner -> EACCES, an unbounded RAM-file write -> EFBIG (not heap OOM-abort), and a child that raises #SS gets killed while the kernel keeps running. Run: tools/qemu_test.py --build --markers-file tools/m6_harden_markers.json --post-boot-delay 3 --settle 4 --cmd-timeout 60 --timeout 260 --boot-timeout 120

required.claim: SpawnArgs validates the user block via the page-walking copy helper and returns EFAULT instead of faulting in ring 0
DrawRect now enforces the display-owner capability like DrawPixel/FbPresent
an unbounded RAM-file write is capped with EFBIG instead of exhausting the kernel heap
a user process that raised #SS was terminated by the kernel, which kept running (fault isolation)
the kernel survived every hostile input and the driver ran to completion

forbidden.why: kernel panic — a userspace action took down the kernel
SpawnArgs did not reject the bad pointer with EFAULT
DrawRect capability gate missing or wrong errno
RAM-file write was not capped with EFBIG
fault isolation did not kill the faulting child as expected
